## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\). The parameter and valid-tuple definitions are source-stated in [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 187-235; 300-304].

The original bigrassmannian hypotheses are
\[
1\le t\le r,\quad 1\le t\le s,\quad r,s\le n,\quad t>r+s-n.
\]
They imply \(r,s<n\): \(r=n\) would imply \(t>s\), contradicting \(t\le s\), and similarly for \(s=n\). Define
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,q-s+t).
\]
Then
\[
t^\vee\ge1\quad(t> s-q),\qquad
t^\vee\le q\quad(t\le s),\qquad
t^\vee\le n-s\quad(t\le r),
\]
and \(1\le q,n-s\le n\). Moreover,
\[
t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)
=(q-s+t)-(q+n-s-n)=t>0.
\]
Thus all conjugated bigrassmannian inequalities hold.

With
\[
i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j),
\]
one has
\[
i^\vee=j,\qquad j^\vee=i,\qquad a^\vee=a,\qquad b^\vee=b.
\]
Also
\[
q-i=t^\vee-1\ge0,\qquad r-j=t-1\ge0,
\]
so
\[
i\le q,\quad j\le r,\quad i+a\le q,\quad j+a\le r,\quad b\le i,j. \tag{*}
\]

The complete family/box enumeration is:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{ambient box}&\text{core}&\text{lower upper shape}&\text{right upper shape}\\ \hline
q^r&i^j&(i^j,b^a)&((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\\
r^q&j^i&(j^i,b^a)&((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})
\end{array}
\]
For the first row, \((*)\) gives: core width/height \(i\le q,j\le r\); lower-shape width \(\max(i,b)=i\le q\), height \(j+a\le r\); right-shape width \(i+a\le q\), height \(j\le r\). Core containment follows from \(b\le i,j\). The second row follows by swapping \(i,j\) and \(q,r\). Hence every partition in each displayed interval lies in its ambient box.

Partition conjugation gives both correspondences:
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}'
=
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})\},
\]
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}'
=
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}.
\]

If \(a\ge1\) and \(1\le N\le ab\), both
\[
(n,r,i,j,a,b,N),\qquad(n,q,j,i,a,b,N)
\]
are valid: every coordinate is positive; \(r<n\) and \(q<n\); the original containment conditions are \(a+j\le r\), \(a+i\le q\); the conjugated ones are respectively \(a+i\le q\), \(a+j\le r\); \(b\le i,j\); and \(1\le N\le ab\).

If \(a=0\), then
\[
a=0\iff q-i=0\ \text{or}\ r-j=0
\iff i=q\ \text{or}\ j=r.
\]
These alternatives interchange under conjugation. Each lower and right upper shape equals its core:
\[
(i^j,b^0)=((i+0)^b,i^{j-b})=i^j,
\]
and likewise for \(j^i\). Thus all four intervals are singleton cores. No valid \(N\) exists, since \(1\le N\le ab=0\) is impossible.

The required computation capability is independently preserved by task-owned artifact `dd8c3f05d598063b3da443dec00d07e26292748e8b66fd64e4cf2300d33856c9`, at `artifacts/computations/dd8c3f05d598063b3da443dec00d07e26292748e8b66fd64e4cf2300d33856c9/artifact.json`: executable-script SHA-256 `7652bda02a7e7899ba48976f1e936807c09934c5b9755bdbf3fd5e4c32d1b554`; input `max_n=12`; exit status \(0\); stdout SHA-256 `7e7fd95e579c7c5d70d2584742008c2c4f8696633e8a21941971c5d10445020a`; empty-stderr SHA-256 `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`. Its captured output reports \(1001\) checked tuples, \(495\) with \(a>0\), \(506\) \(a=0\) cases, and `RESULT PASS`. This finite audit is only a check; the symbolic argument proves the universal certificate.

Conclusion: the standalone admissibility certificate is established. No minimality or parent-theorem claim is inferred.
